newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola Bottling profits surge in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Bottling profits surge in 1996.

text.p: Coca-Cola Bottling Co. Consolidated said Friday its fiscal 1996 profits surged more than 50 percent as sales of all its major beverages, led by Sprite, continued to grow.

The company, which bottles products for the Coca-Cola Co., said it earned $16.2 million, or $1.74 per share, in 1996, even after it took a non-cash, after-tax charge of $2.7 million for a retirement benefit awarded to J. Frank Harrison Jr., who quit as chairman in December after two decades in the post.
In 1995, the Charlotte, N.C.-based company earned $10.5 million, or $1.13 per share, after a one-time charge of $5 million to retire debt early.
Net sales edged up about 2 percent to $773.8 million in 1996 from $761.9 million, as a 4 percent rise in franchise sales was partly offset by lower contract sales.
Coca-Coca Bottling said its core brands all had solid sales growth during 1996, and those trends have accelerated during the first quarter of 1997.
Sprite in particular grew rapidly during 1996, achieving a double-digit pace, the company said.
Gross margin grew by 7.5 percent, mainly due to lower packaging costs as well as the growth in franchise volume.
Separately, Embotelladora Andina SA, Coca-Cola Co.'s largest Chilean bottler, said the beverage giant had raised its stake in the company to 11 percent from 6 percent.
The company said it has sold 17,962,864 shares to Coca-Cola for $98.5 million.
Andina also has plants in Argentina and Brazil.
Coca-Cola Bottling's stock dropped $1.50 to $44 on Nasdaq in midafternoon trading.
